description.p: Case Maker draws a 3D-printable enclosure around a board you actually have. Pick the board from the library, or import its dimensions, and the case is generated around its real connectors and mounting holes instead of being guessed from a photo.

ul.li: Thirty built-in boards, with the connector, hole and clearance data each one needs, plus anything you import or enable from a community library.
Port cutouts that move with the board: toggle a USB or HDMI opening and the shell rebuilds in a few milliseconds.
Joints, lids, dividers, magnets, mounting plates and rack shelves, all parametric.
Export to STL or 3MF for a slicer.

description.p: The same program can drive a Makera Z1 desktop CNC: it plans the job, simulates the stock it removes, checks the program against the machine's own limits and posts a verified file.
It runs entirely on your own computer. No account, no cloud: the app serves its own interface from its own embedded server, and a browser on the same network can open it and drive the same machine.
The first Case Maker release for Linux.
